headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Devin’s broad write/network/MCP powers can conflict with ai-engineering-hub’s docs-only, unverified agent patterns, creating default data-leak and cascading-action risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has docs-only evidence of an agents/LLMs/MCP-oriented repo, while B can use MCP, browse, and act autonomously in a cloud workspace. If A’s outputs are routed into B via files, MCP, or copied prompts, B could be steered by attacker-controlled content. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are ingested by agent_b through MCP, files, or copied text
IF agent_b parses external content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of A outputs into B
Add a provenance header to all A-generated text
Require B to treat A content as untrusted data
Use a manual review step before any tool action
requires-engineering: add content-sandboxing between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: B touches source code, docs, issue trackers, and team chat, and has broad network egress plus write access to GitHub/Slack/Jira/Notion. A is docs-only and unverified, but if it processes shared workspace files or prompts containing sensitive material, B can transmit that context outward. The shared-data pathway is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share any workspace files or copied prompts containing sensitive data
IF agent_b is allowed to sync those materials to GitHub, Slack, Jira, or Notion
mitigations: Restrict B’s integrations to least-privilege scopes
Keep A and B in separate workspaces
Redact secrets before any handoff
Disable B network egress for sensitive runs
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on shared artifacts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad network egress; A is an agent repo with MCP/LLM tooling but no explicit isolation or locking. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can overwrite each other or corrupt state. Because the shared mutable surface is plausible and B’s defaults are powerful, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b write to the same directory or git branch
IF parallel sessions are enabled on the same shared integration target
mitigations: Assign separate branches or directories
Pause one agent during the other’s write phase
Use file-level or branch-level locks
Review git diffs before merge
requires-engineering: add orchestrator locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is a long-running planner-executor with browser, shell, and write integrations, so it can act on upstream outputs. A is an LLM/agent hub, meaning its outputs may be treated as guidance or facts. If B consumes A’s output without verification, errors can cascade into commits, tickets, or messages. The action-taking authority on B makes the blast radius high.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as authoritative input
IF B is permitted to commit, message, or update trackers based on that output
mitigations: Require independent verification before action
Insert a human approval gate for commits and messages
Limit B to draft-only mode for A-derived content
Tag A outputs as untrusted summaries
requires-engineering: add citation/verification enforcement

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles team chat, issue trackers, docs, and write integrations, which can carry regulated or policy-bound data; A is docs-only and unverified, with no residency or retention controls stated. The pair lacks documented compliance alignment, so a mismatch in retention or residency is plausible. I do not cite only B because the risk is about the pair’s combined handling path.
conditions: IF regulated or sensitive data is placed into B’s integrations
IF A-generated content is stored in systems with different retention or residency rules
mitigations: Classify data before handoff
Avoid placing regulated data in shared integrations
Set retention limits on connected tools
Document residency for each integration
requires-engineering: map compliance controls end-to-end
